name: a single-line column repeats its value down every rung beside a ladder column (executed-result parity)
description: Seed one player, one 2023 REG week 1 game, a THREE-rung FanDuel GAME_ALT_PASSING_YARDS ladder at 199.5/249.5/299.5, and beside it a single-line FanDuel market posting 262.5. The single-line column takes the family default market by naming no market_type. Under an active line axis it must REPEAT its 262.5 down every rung, which is what every non-axis column already does under the week axis, and what makes the standard line usable as the comparison point next to a ladder. It previously rendered NULL on all three, because the join correlated EVERY betting column on selection_metric_line rather than only the ladder ones -- so a single-line column matched only where its own line numerically coincided with a rung, which is a coincidence-of-numerals join and the exact mistake the different-quantity refusal exists to prevent. The oracle asserts the axis rung label beside both columns, so a regression that blanks the standard column and one that mislabels the row are separately visible.
